correctness.rationale: For the shortness rule (leading 1 and second digit 0 or 1), classify representations by final digit: for even 2m the final digit must be 0 and g(2m)=g(m); for odd 2m+1≥3, last +1 and −1 contribute opposite signs so g(2m+1)=g(m)−g(m+1). With g(1)=g(2)=1, v(n)=(g(n),g(n+1)) evolves by (a,a−b) for a trailing 0 and (a−b,b) for trailing 1. These unimodular actions preserve coprimality, so the projective states P(equal), I(b=0), Z(a=0), X(negative or 0<a/b<1) cover all possibilities; X absorbs. The exact automaton recognizes g(n)=0 precisely at ordinary binary words 1(01*0)*10*. Counting paths gives F_{r−1} balanced r-bit numbers and F_{r+1}−1 below 2^r, density 0 and exponent log_2 φ. Independent literal enumeration and recurrence automaton comparisons tested n≤240. They do not substitute for the proof for all n.
